NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.“Kya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)” Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.“We had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,” she explained.Modi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.“To be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,” he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics. Modi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.“Itne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),” Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.“I was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.“There were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,” she said.The meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.“During the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),” he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.“I have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.“Far more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,” Modi said.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time. India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.

Article Title: ‘From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping’: PM Modi’s heartfelt message to CWG heroes - Watch
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi interacted with India's CWG 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday. (Pic credit: PM Modi's X post)

Mirabai recalls four years of struggle

‘One family will bring three medals’

NEW DELHI: “From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping.”Prime Minister Narendra Modi had an emotional message for Mirabai Chanu as he interacted with India's Commonwealth Games 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday, reflecting on the sacrifices behind the country's successful campaign in Glasgow.Modi hosted the medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg and heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys at the Games. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings.During one of the conversations, Modi recalled the emotional scenes surrounding Mirabai's gold-medal triumph.“Tears were falling from you. I feel as if from every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping,” Modi told the Olympic silver medallist.Mirabai, who won gold in Glasgow, opened up about the difficult journey that preceded her Commonwealth Games triumph, including the disappointment of the Paris Olympics.“I was very happy, and emotional too. That day the happiness was greater and I cried because at the Paris Olympics, I lost a medal by 1 kg. In a player’s life what all we have to face. So within these 4 years, how much and what all I had faced, every time injuries were going on and all that was happening.So with great difficulty I had faced these 4 years. So when all that happened, on the podium when I stood, sir, and when our flag goes up and our national anthem plays, sir, we cannot stop, sir, tears come out on their own,” she said.Modi responded by highlighting the wider impact of the athletes' achievements.“This is very good. It is not as if this achievement of yours is considered only your achievement; your victory becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations.”The informal interaction also saw athletes share lighter and deeply personal moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Modi reminded para shot put gold medallist Sharmila Dhankar of a promise she had made earlier.“You made a promise. Last time, yours, both daughters will become players,” Modi said with a smile.Dhankar replied: “Haanji, right now they are young in age. In the next Commonwealth, one family will bring 3 medals.”Men's 100m T47 gold medallist Dilip Gavit, meanwhile, spoke about dedicating his performance to his guru.“When I was running, when my event was on 29th (July), that day was Guru Purnima, so that day I gave a gift to my guru,” he was heard saying in the video.In another video posted by Modi, gold medallist boxer Sakshi Chaudhary introduced herself and the contingent.“Hello friends! This is Sakshi Chaudhary. Today, our honourable Prime Minister has invited us, the Commonwealth Games medalists, and we feel very proud. We are extremely happy to have met him; he is very humble. Sir, would you like to say something?” she said.Modi replied with a message that summed up his interaction with the athletes: “Jo khelega, woh khilega” (The one who plays, will blossom). “Always cheer for Bharat.”India's fourth-place finish came despite a significantly smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme compared to Birmingham 2022. India sent 122 athletes to Glasgow, compared to 210 in Birmingham, while 30 of its 61 medals in 2022 came in sports that were not part of the Glasgow programme.Despite those limitations, India retained its fourth-place position and improved its medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with medals. Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh was the only Indian athlete to win two medals.The Glasgow Games concluded after 11 days, with Scotland handing over the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India ahead of the 2030 edition in Ahmedabad.The symbols were handed to Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi during the closing ceremony.Ahmedabad will become only the second Indian city to host the Commonwealth Games after New Delhi staged the 2010 edition.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi hosted medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg. Modi heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze.

Article Title: From hospital bed to CWG gold: How Jaismine Lamboria fought the odds in Glasgow
Article Text:
India's Jaismine Lamboria celebrates after winning the women's 57kg boxing final. (AP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Just weeks before stepping into the ring at the Commonwealth Games, Jaismine Lamboria wasn’t thinking about medals. She was searching for answers. The recurring fever had refused to go away.Multiple medical tests showed nothing unusual and the Indian boxer tried to push through, managing the symptoms with paracetamol. When the illness persisted, she was admitted to a hospital in Mohali. Doctors finally diagnosed a bacterial infection, putting her on an intensive 14-day course of medication. For an athlete preparing for one of the biggest competitions of the year, it could easily have been the end of the campaign.Instead, it became the beginning of one of the most remarkable comebacks of her career. “I was avoiding further medical tests because the initial reports were coming back normal. We didn’t know what exactly had to be treated. Finally, after I was admitted, they detected a bacterial infection and I was on medication for 14 days,” the 57kg boxer said.When she was discharged, the clock was already ticking. Barely three weeks remained before the Games.“I started training only on July 1. Initially it was just warm-up, walking and stretching. I had very little time, so we had to be patient.”The physical recovery was only one part of the challenge. During those uncertain weeks, sports psychologist Priya Vrinda became a constant source of support, ensuring the illness didn’t break her confidence.“When I was sick, I was already connected with Priya Vrinda ma’am. She kept me mentally strong and never allowed me to go down,” Jaismine said. That resilience was evident when she returned to competition. Jaismine boxed with maturity, tactical discipline and composure to upgrade the Commonwealth bronze she had won four years ago into gold in the 57kg.One of Jaismine’s biggest assets inside the ring has been her reach in her category. While every opponent may not be shorter — Jaismine stands five feet seven inches in her socks — she believes her physical advantage has become an important weapon thanks to careful coaching. “My coaches taught me how to use my reach properly. It definitely gives me an advantage in many bouts.”
Article Summary: Jaismine Lamboria won gold in the women's 57kg boxing at the Commonwealth Games. The Indian boxer had been suffering from a recurring fever. Doctors diagnosed a bacterial infection and put her on a 14-day course of medication. Jaismine credits her coach Priya Vrinda with helping her recover.

Article Title: How Jadumani Singh's risky weight change nearly derailed his CWG dream before winning Glasgow silver
Article Text:
India's Jadumani Singh Mandengbam (PTI Photo)

A bold gamble after the 50kg category disappeared

The selection maze before Glasgow

Jadumani Si​ngh's Road to CWG Silver (AI-generated Infographic)

The Sports Ministry hurdle

Jadumani Singh Mandengbam (PTI Photo)

Why the gold slipped away

File Pic: L Sarita Devi (PTI Photo)

Olympic gold remains the ultimate dream

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: When Indian pugilist Jadumani Singh Mandengbam stepped onto the podium to receive the men's 55kg silver medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, it marked the culmination of a journey that had almost ended before it had even begun.The 22-year-old Manipuri boxer was one of India's standout performers, winning four consecutive unanimous 5-0 verdicts to storm into the bantamweight final before settling for silver against Australia's Jye Dixon. His medal also formed part of India's historic boxing campaign, which yielded seven golds and three silvers, making the country the No. 1 boxing nation at the Games for the first time.Yet, behind that success lay months of uncertainty, selection hurdles and a weight-category gamble that nearly cost him a place on the flight to Scotland.Speaking exclusively to TimesofIndia.com, former world champion and Jadumani's mentor, Laishram Sarita Devi, recounted how the young boxer refused to abandon his Olympic dream even when every obstacle seemed stacked against him.Jadumani had built his reputation in the 50kg category, winning medals at World Boxing Cups before learning that the division would no longer feature in the Commonwealth Games, Asian Games or Olympic programme.Rather than remain in a non-Olympic category, he decided to move up to 55kg — a division already occupied by some of India's biggest names."He continued to consult with me. Whenever he had to make a big decision, he called up and consulted with me — like increasing his weight category," Sarita told TimesofIndia.com."After he won a World Cup medal in 50kg, he got to know that the weight category is no longer in the CWG, Asian Games and Olympics. He wanted to move to 55kg."The decision immediately brought fresh challenges."Army had their No. 1 boxer in the 55kg category in Pune, who is Services' No. 1 boxer. And the weight category also has Amit Panghal — Olympian and Asian champion. He said he wanted to move up the weight to compete at CWG, Asian Games etc, but was discouraged by hearing questions like whether he would be able to compete at that level, which created a doubt in him," she said.Sarita, however, wanted only one answer: "We sat down and I asked him, 'Are you confident about the decision?' He said he was, so I told him to move up the category."The decision created another problem.Without competing in the National Championships, Jadumani could not enter the national coaching camp. But because he belonged to the Army Sports Institute, Services already had its designated 55kg representative. Attempts to let him represent Manipur also failed."We tried to make him compete for the state of Manipur, but we didn't get an NOC because he is with the Army," Sarita said.Relief finally arrived through a Boxing Federation of India (BFI) policy that granted direct entries to the National Championships for World Boxing Cup medallists. The move was aimed at rewarding elite international performers and ensuring they were not blocked by the usual domestic qualification pathways.The decision allowed Jadumani to compete directly in the 55kg draw despite the institutional overlap, resulting in multiple squad members — Pawan Bartwal, Jadumani Singh and Amit Panghal — finding themselves in the same weight-category draw.Sarita said her ward grabbed the opportunity with both hands."He then got a chance to compete in 55kg in the Nationals. Due to his effort, he won against the Services No.1, Olympians etc to be named Best Boxer in the Nationals. After that he got the chance to be part of the India camp," she said.He then cleared the final selection trials, which included physical assessments alongside ring performances."He participated in the final trial for the CWG and Asian Games — which had many aspects like strength and endurance tests before fighting in the ring. He won all of it to get selected for the CWG and was really happy and started training hard," she added.Just when Glasgow appeared certain, another setback emerged.Because Jadumani had only recently moved into 55kg, he did not possess the Asian ranking required under the Sports Ministry's eligibility criteria for Commonwealth Games selection."He got an explanation mail from the Sports Ministry, which put him in immense tension ahead of the Games," Sarita recalled.Under the ministry's guidelines, boxers were expected to be ranked among Asia's top eight in their respective categories."He was ranked No. 2 in 50kg, but he lacked a ranking in the new 55kg category. He had only competed in one Asian Championship in the new weight category before the trials for CWG and, being new to the category, lost in the quarterfinals," she said.That led to fresh doubts over his selection."He was disheartened when questions were raised whether he was a medal prospect because he was not in the rankings prescribed by the ministry. He called me and said the coaches were saying he may or may not be on the flight to the CWG because of this letter from the ministry," she recalled.The uncertainty only ended after BFI submitted a detailed explanation to the ministry, outlining Jadumani's circumstances following his weight-category switch."BFI replied to the ministry properly, explaining everything and after a lot of effort his ticket to Glasgow was approved. What I like about him is that he is the kind of person who doesn't give up and has a very strong will power," she said.Jadumani eventually reached the final after four demanding contests, each won by an identical 5-0 margin. But Sarita believes the scheduling ultimately worked against him."Jadumani's four bouts were very tough. He played all out in all the bouts till the semifinals as he got proper rest and recovery time. Since the gold medal opponent got a bye earlier, he had fewer bouts than Jadumani," she explained.The semifinal-final turnaround, she felt, proved decisive. There was a one-day gap after every bout until the semifinals, but there was no gap between the semifinal and final in Glasgow."Jadumani fought his semifinal in the evening and got the final bout the next morning only, so he did not get much time for recovery. If it was in the evening, he could have fought better. When he entered the ring for the final, I saw his face and body language sitting here and realised he had not had enough recovery," she said.The experience, she believes, underlines the growing importance of sports science."In such situations, we should look for how we can enhance or speed up the recovery process through sports science. We should discuss it to make sure our boxers can give 100 per cent every time they enter the ring," she added.Sarita first noticed Jadumani as a youngster competing in a local tournament."When I saw Jadumani for the first time, it was a tournament for young boys. His movement was really pleasing and I thought he could become a good boxer in the future. I identified him at that time only and gave him Rs 500 because I was very pleased with his performance," she recalled."Jadumani did not start with me from the grassroots. He learnt his basics from another academy. He came to my academy when he was preparing to enrol in the Army Sports Institute in Pune. At that time, I did not have any infrastructure and was coaching from a makeshift setup. And then Covid happened, we had to train in a very isolated small makeshift place,” she added.Years later, after training together through difficult Covid-19 conditions and watching him overcome one hurdle after another, Sarita believes Glasgow is only the beginning."We missed gold at the CWG, but we will work hard to get gold at the Asian Games for sure," she said.The bigger ambition, however, stretches far beyond continental success."His first and primary target remains Olympic gold. Commonwealth Games and Asian Games are the stepping stones in that journey. He will try to win India's first Olympic gold medal in boxing," Sarita concluded.
Article Summary: Jadumani Singh Mandengbam won silver at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The 22-year-old Manipuri boxer won four consecutive unanimous 5-0 verdicts to storm into the bantamweight final before settling for silver against Australia's Jye Dixon. His medal also formed part of India's historic boxing campaign, which yielded seven golds and three silvers, making the country the No. 1 boxing nation at the Games.

Article Title: Days after historic CWG gold, Dilip Gavit leaves without meeting Raj Thackeray after two-hour wait
Article Text:
India's Dilip Mahadu Gavit (PTI Photo)

Invited, but left waiting

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A champion who made history in Glasgow

A journey built on resilience

Just days after scripting history for Indian para athletics at the Commonwealth Games, gold medallist Dilip Gavit found himself making headlines for a very different reason. The 23-year-old sprinter, who became India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medallist in the men's 100m T47 event, waited for nearly two hours to meet Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray in Nashik on Thursday before leaving without the meeting taking place.According to Gavit's coach quoted by PTI, Vaijanath Kale, the para-athlete had been invited to meet Thackeray during the MNS chief's visit to Nashik. However, despite arriving at the scheduled venue, Gavit and his coach were made to wait for nearly two hours. A video from the venue showed MNS workers requesting the duo to wait longer while trying to explain that Thackeray was occupied."We were waiting for quite some time... Sir is busy. We will meet him later," Kale is heard saying in the video before they eventually left.The incident came just days after Gavit delivered one of India's biggest moments at the Commonwealth Games. Clocking a Games-record 10.71 seconds, the Nashik sprinter won the men's 100m T47 gold medal, leading a historic Indian one-two finish alongside Mohammed Basil Morssinganakath, who claimed silver. The victory marked India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medal in para athletics 100m T47.Gavit's success carries a deeper significance given his remarkable journey. Born into an economically disadvantaged tribal family in Maharashtra, he lost his right arm in a childhood accident. His life changed when coach Vaijanath Kale took him under his wing at the age of 12, supporting his education and athletic development. After winning gold in Glasgow, Gavit emotionally dedicated the medal to Kale, crediting his coach for transforming his life.
Article Summary: Dilip Gavit was invited to meet Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray. The 23-year-old sprinter waited for nearly two hours for the meeting to take place. The incident came just days after he became India's first Commonwealth Games gold medallist in the men's 100m T47 event.

Article Title: How Harsh fought through pain to script CWG history, now targets Asiad medal
Article Text:
How judoka Harsh overcame pain

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Harsh Singh's right knee still swells. It still hurts. Every time the Indian judoka steps onto the mat, he is reminded of the ACL and meniscus tear that nearly derailed his career. But at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, pain took a back seat as the 23-year-old scripted history by becoming India's first-ever men's judo gold medallist."The pain never really goes away," Singh told TOI in an interview on Thursday. "Sometimes my knee still swells up and feels tight. During the CWG, I felt the pain and the knee occasionally got swollen. After surgery, the joint never became exactly the way it was before. There's always a little discomfort during fights. You have to ignore it and continue. The medal kept me going."The historic triumph came less than a year after Singh tore his ACL and meniscus while training at the Inspire Institute of Sport (IIS) in Aug 2025. Surgery followed in Oct last in Bengaluru before a year-long rehabilitation helped him return to competition."I was in rehabilitation for almost a year. The entire coaching team at the IIS, recovery specialists and Spencer sir (Mackay, S&C expert) helped me throughout.They rebuilt my strength step by step. Because of the IIS and their entire team, I was able to come back on the mat, qualify for the CWG and represent India," he said.The comeback demanded another battle off the mat. Months away from competition saw his weight rise to nearly 72kg, forcing him to shed more than 12kg to return to his 60kg category. Gold at a ranking tournament and bronze at the senior National championships sealed his place in India's CWG squad.Despite lingering discomfort, Singh dominated in Glasgow, with only a hard-fought semifinal stretching him before he clinched the historic title."The semifinal (against the Australian Pedro Carlos) was the toughest. In the 60kg category, even a small point can decide the match. We didn't want to concede anything and stayed aggressive," he recalled.With CWG gold secured, Singh has already shifted his attention to next year's Asian Games. Training stints in Japan and South Korea are part of his preparations as he looks to bridge the gap with Asia's best."I want to improve my speed, grip and strength. Japanese and Korean players are very fast, so training there will help," he said.Born into a modest family, with his father working as a daily-wage labourer, Singh once trained without owning a judo uniform. Support from the govt's schemes and a privately funded athletes' training centre changed the course of his career."My life has changed because of this medal. More people have started noticing judo," he said. "But the best compliment came from my family. They told me, 'You have made the entire family proud.' That meant more than anything else."Having conquered injury to create CWG history, Singh's next aim is clear — turning a gritty comeback into an Asian Games podium finish.
Article Summary: Harsh Singh became India's first-ever men's judo gold medallist. The 23-year-old tore his ACL and meniscus while training at the Inspire Institute of Sport. Surgery followed in Oct last in Bengaluru before a year-long rehabilitation helped him return to competition.

Article Title: 'I worked tirelessly while staying in Pakistan': Arshad Nadeem blames Glasgow cold for CWG poor show
Article Text:
Arshad Nadeem (AFP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lausanne Diamond League next

Pakistan’s Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem has blamed the cold Glasgow weather for his disappointing performance at the Commonwealth Games. The defending champion finished ninth after failing to make the final three rounds, saying the low temperature made his body stiff and affected his usually smooth run-up.Nadeem managed 77.41 metres with his second throw after opening with a foul. His third attempt was 75.39m, leaving him outside the top eight.“The weather was extremely cold and I personally felt that it affected my body. As you have seen in many of my previous competitions, my run-up is usually very smooth, but this time it wasn’t… because my body had become stiff due to the cold conditions. My fitness was good and my health was fine, but ultimately whatever Allah wills is what happens,” he told reporters on Wednesday.Despite the result, Nadeem said he remains determined to make a strong comeback and urged fans to continue supporting him.“Please don’t lose heart and don’t stop supporting me either. Whatever I have achieved has only been possible because Allah blessed me with the opportunity to do it. The respect and recognition Pakistan has received around the world have come through years of hard work. I worked tirelessly while staying in Pakistan,” he added.“God willing, I will prepare with full dedication for the upcoming competitions and once again raise Pakistan’s flag on the international stage.”Nadeem also responded to criticism on social media, saying he understood the disappointment among Pakistani fans.“I have heard many things on social media, but I want everyone to remember that I am Pakistan’s son, and I always will be,” he maintained.Nadeem’s next challenge will be the Lausanne Diamond League in Switzerland on August 21. He will face a strong field that includes India’s Neeraj Chopra , Commonwealth champion Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, Keshorn Walcott, Anderson Peters and Thomas Rohler.Nadeem will hope to regain his form before the Asian Games later this year.
Article Summary: Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem has blamed the cold Glasgow weather for his disappointing performance at the Commonwealth Games. The defending champion finished ninth after failing to make the final three rounds. He said the low temperature made his body stiff and affected his usually smooth run-up.

Article Title: Glasgow to Ahmedabad: Gujarat receives Commonwealth Games flag as 2030 countdown begins
Article Text:
Neeraj Chopra, left, hands over the Commonwealth Games Federation flag to Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president P T Usha during the closing ceremony of the 23rd Commonwealth Games (CWG), at OVO Hydro, in Glasgow, Scotland. (PTI)

The Commonwealth Games flag was formally presented to Gujarat chief minister Bhupendra Patel on Wednesday, marking the beginning of preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.After returning from Glasgow, deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi handed over the flag to Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar.Sanghavi had attended the closing ceremony of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Sunday along with Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha. During the ceremony, the Commonwealth Games flag was officially handed over to India as Ahmedabad prepares to host the next edition in 2030.According to an official release, "deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi formally presented the Commonwealth Games Flag, with full honour and dignity, to chief minister Bhupendra Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar."Para-athletes Rakesh Bhatt and Rohit Majgul, who represented Gujarat at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, were present during the ceremony. Para table tennis player Sonal Patel also attended.The release added, "The Commonwealth Games Flag will now remain in Gujarat until the 2030 Commonwealth Games. Along with advancing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Fit India' vision, it will serve as an inspiration for athletes and symbolise the commencement of preparations for the upcoming event."Speaking to reporters after arriving at Ahmedabad Airport earlier in the day, Sanghavi said the city aims to set a new standard for hosting the Commonwealth Games."These Games will be organised with grandeur and with the best possible arrangements for the athletes. They will be conducted in such a way that every athlete can deliver his best performance," the deputy CM said.Sanghavi, who also holds the sports portfolio, said the Gujarat government remains committed to taking forward Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Fit India movement and anti-drug campaign."We will advance the anti-drug campaign and the Fit India Movement so that the youth of the country receive maximum opportunities in the sports sector. The Gujarat Government is working towards this goal. Under the guidance of the Government of India, we will continue to move this work forward," he said.

Deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi handed over the flag to Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar. Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha attended the ceremony.

Article Title: Reality check after Commonwealth Games 2026: India’s boxing renaissance to face ultimate Asian exam
Article Text:
New Delhi, Aug 04 (ANI): Union Minister Kiren Rijiju in a group photograph with Indian boxing contingent (@KirenRijiju X/ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India’s record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism, but the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. After returning from Glasgow with a historic haul of seven gold and three silver medals, India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.The CWG triumph underlined the country’s growing depth, particularly in women’s boxing. Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg), Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg) and Arundhati Choudhary (70kg) struck gold, while Sachin Siwach (60kg) and Ankush Panghal (80kg) topped the podium in the men’s competition. Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain, Jadumani Singh and Narender Berwal added silver medals.The challenge in Aichi-Nagoya, however, will be on an entirely different scale. Unlike the Commonwealth Games, the Asian Games will feature continental powerhouses such as Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, China, Chinese Taipei, Japan and North Korea — nations that have consistently dominated the World Championships and the Olympics.Uzbek stars Mirazizbek Mirzakhalilov and Bobo-Usmon Baturov, along with Kazakhstan’s Kairat Yeraliyev and Ablaikhan Zhussupov, are expected to headline a field packed with world-class talent.India will also be without two of its Commonwealth champions. Jaismine (57kg) and Arundhati (70kg) will miss out because their weight categories do not feature in the Asian Games programme, depriving the country of two genuine medal prospects.“The Asian Games for us is like the Olympics,” Boxing Federation of India president Ajay Singh said. “The best teams in the world today are Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and India, and all three are in Asia. Add a strong Chinese contingent and you understand why it is much tougher. You can’t replicate this (CWG) performance at the Asian Games. But if you win a sizeable number of medals at the Asian Games, you can be hopeful of winning medals at the Olympics too.Women’s head coach Santiago Nieva shared a similar assessment while insisting the team remains on the right path.“We can’t guarantee that we will win gold all the time, but we are on the right track. We know how strong the field will be at the Asian Games. The boxers are aware that they can’t sit on their success,” he said.India had returned with one silver and three bronze medals from the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. The Glasgow CWG showcased the strides the boxing contingent has made. But it’ll be Aichi-Nagoya that is going to reveal whether the progress is enough to challenge Asia’s finest and signal genuine medal potential for the 2028 Olympics.
Article Summary: India's record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism. But the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.

Article Title: Pakistan boxer Qudratullah ‘goes missing’ in Glasgow after Commonwealth Games campaign
Article Text:
Pakistan boxer Qudratullah

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistani boxer Qudratullah has reportedly gone missing in Glasgow, just hours before the country’s Commonwealth Games contingent was scheduled to leave for home.According to a report by Pakistani outlet Geo News, sources in the Pakistan Boxing Federation said Qudratullah was last seen in his hotel room at around 2am. Officials later checked his room and found that he was no longer there.The Pakistan team was due to gather in the hotel lobby at 9am before leaving for Pakistan. However, Qudratullah could not be found when officials checked his room, sources said.His passport and return ticket are reportedly still with the team manager. The incident is not the first such case involving a Pakistani boxer abroad, with another promising boxer, Zohaib, reportedly going missing during an international tour of Italy last year.Pakistan’s 21-member contingent finished the 2026 Commonwealth Games with only one medal. Boxer Fatima Zahra won bronze in the women’s 60kg category, giving Pakistan its only podium finish at the Games.The result was Pakistan’s lowest medal tally since the 1998 Commonwealth Games, when the country won one silver. Pakistan had also returned without a medal from the 1990 edition, making Glasgow its poorest CWG campaign in 36 years.Fatima made history by becoming the first Pakistani female boxer to win a Commonwealth Games medal and was later chosen to carry the national flag at the closing ceremony.Pakistan’s biggest medal hope, Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem, also failed to finish on the podium after serving as the country’s flagbearer at the opening ceremony.
Article Summary: Qudratullah was last seen in his hotel room at around 2am. Pakistan team was due to gather in the hotel lobby at 9am before leaving for Pakistan. Pakistan’s 21-member contingent finished the 2026 Commonwealth Games with only one medal.

Article Title: ‘Like preparing for IIT and UPSC together’: Father Murali shares Sreeshankar’s comeback story
Article Text:
Murali Sreeshankar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOCHI: S Murali gave an unusual analogy to describe the struggles his son, long jumper Sreeshankar Murali, undertook to regain full fitness after a career-threatening knee injury he sustained two years ago.“Sreeshankar’s comeback was as difficult as preparing for the IIT and Civil Services simultaneously,” he told TOI.Murali is currently near Prague, where he is closely monitoring his son’s training ahead of a busy stretch that begins with the World Athletics Continental Tour (silver level) meet in Bhubaneswar on Aug 22, followed by next month’s Asian Games in Japan.“Sreeshankar’s training now revolves around strength and conditioning, along with the prehab and rehab programme designed by coach Wayne Lombard. There is very little time to work on technique. The priority is to protect the knee on his take-off leg,” Murali said.His IIT-UPSC analogy aptly captures the magnitude of the challenge Sreeshankar faced after suffering the devastating injury just months before the 2024 Paris Olympics.Two years later, the journey came full circle when the 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.“Of all the medals Sreeshankar has won, this one gives me the greatest satisfaction because of the circumstances under which he achieved it. It reflects his mental toughness and hunger,” Murali said.The conditions in Glasgow were anything but favourable.“It was around 12 degrees Celsius with drizzle and strong winds, making the runway tricky,” Murali said. Despite the difficult conditions, Sreeshankar produced a best jump of 8.09m to finish second.The performance inevitably brought back painful memories of 2024, when the family received a grim diagnosis after Sreeshankar tore the patellar tendon in his take-off leg.“The doctors in Mumbai had not seen an injury like this. I thought he would never be able to walk again,” Murali recalled.“They told us it wasn’t a common sports injury but the kind usually seen after a serious car accident. His knee was completely ruptured.”Determined to find the best treatment, Murali travelled nearly 1,900 miles with his son to Doha’s Aspetar Hospital. “The surgeons reconstructed his knee using four screws.”The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process.The painstaking recovery paid rich dividends. Since returning to elite competition, Sreeshankar has consistently cleared the eight-metre mark, including a season’s best of 8.38m at the Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar in June.“There is no time to bask in the Commonwealth Games glory,” Murali said, pointing to the demanding schedule ahead.Sreeshankar will now turn his attention to the Asian Games in Japan, where he hopes to upgrade the silver medal he won at the previous edition in Hangzhou.“With everything Sreeshankar has gone through, he has every reason to believe he can stand on top of the podium at the Asian Games,” Murali concluded.
Article Summary: Sreeshankar Murali suffered a career-threatening knee injury two years ago. The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process. The 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week's Commonwealth Games.

Article Title: 'You are still a role model': CWG medallist Tejaswin Shankar hails Vinesh Phogat, recalls 2018 memories
Article Text:
Tejaswin Shankar and Vinesh Phogat

Commonwealth Games 2026 bronze medallist Tejaswin Shankar has expressed his gratitude to star wrestler Vinesh Phogat for her words of encouragement after a knee injury forced him to withdraw from the high jump event at the recent Commonwealth Games.Shankar, a two-time Commonwealth Games medallist, was forced out of the high jump after his long-standing knee problem flared up during his opening attempt. The setback left the athlete devastated, with Shankar breaking down in tears after being unable to continue.Despite the disappointment, he bounced back strongly in the gruelling two-day decathlon, finishing with 7,976 points and securing his second Commonwealth Games medal. His national record in the decathlon stands at 8,057 points.Shankar has been dealing with chronic patellar tendinitis, commonly known as jumper’s knee.Following his withdrawal, Vinesh had reached out to him with a motivational message, urging him to remain focused and prepared for whatever came next.“Teju, you still can do it. Stay focused on what is ahead," Vinesh wrote on X. "My coach always said, as professional athletes, we must always be prepared for the best and at the same time, be ready for the worst.In life, everything happened for a reason, I guess. Rooting for you as always."Remembering Vinesh’s support, Shankar thanked her publicly and recalled how she had helped him feel comfortable during his first Commonwealth Games in 2018.Remembering her support, Shankar replied, “Thank you, Vinesh ji for your motivating words. I remember my first CWG in 2018 as a teenager when you made me feel comfortable and told me that I belonged there. 8 years later, you are still a role model."Meanwhile, Vinesh said the women wrestlers who accused former Wrestling Federation of India chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh of sexual harassment will appeal a Delhi court’s decision to acquit him.A Delhi court on Monday acquitted Brij Bhushan and co-accused Vinod Tomar in the sexual harassment case filed by the women wrestlers. Vinesh confirmed that the wrestlers would challenge the verdict.

Article Title: Brazil footballer falls into tunnel while celebrating goal, suffers ankle injury - Watch
Article Text:
Video/screengrab

A goal celebration in Brazil's top-flight football competition took an unexpected turn after Coritiba defender Jacy Maranhão fell into a tunnel beside the pitch and injured his ankle.Jacy, 29, was celebrating after heading Coritiba into a 2-0 lead against Chapecoense in the 41st minute of their Brazilian Serie A match. The defender picked up the ball and ran towards a group of supporters, jumping as he celebrated.However, his celebration ended when he fell through an opening and into a dark passageway next to the pitch.Jacy was able to get back onto the field after the fall and continued playing into the first few minutes of the second half. He was then substituted because of the ankle injury he suffered during the incident.The situation became more frustrating for the Coritiba defender when VAR reviewed his goal and ruled that he had been offside. The goal was subsequently disallowed.Despite losing Jacy, Coritiba went on to beat Chapecoense 2-1.The incident was not the first time a footballer has fallen into the passageway at Estádio Major Antônio Couto Pereira.In 2014, Cameroon striker Joel also jumped over the barriers while celebrating during Coritiba's 3-1 win over Sao Paulo. He fell into the same tunnel during that incident.Brazilian journalist Leonardo Mendes Jr later pointed out what he described as an unusual link between the two incidents."There's one detail that makes it even more unbelievable," he posted on social media."Jacy repeats the jump in Joel's tunnel: the security guard who tries to prevent the jump is the same one!"
Article Summary: Coritiba defender Jacy Maranhão fell into a tunnel beside the pitch. Jacy, 29, was celebrating after heading Coritiba into a 2-0 lead against Chapecoense. He was substituted because of the ankle injury he suffered during the incident.
